displayName: Progress OpenEdge ABL → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3
description: Progress OpenEdge ABL (the 4GL, .p/.w/.i files) migrating to Java 21 + Spring Boot 3. This is the Tier-2 'talent-extinction' technology: the ABL developer pool is retiring, so behavioural specs must be captured now. ABL's idiom gap to Java is wide and specific: in-memory TEMP-TABLEs with indexes, implicit record buffers with lock modes (NO-LOCK / EXCLUSIVE-LOCK / SHARE-LOCK), block-scoped TRANSACTIONs (no explicit begin/commit), SHARED / GLOBAL variables that couple procedures, NO-ERROR error suppression + ERROR-STATUS, the Unknown value (?) that is distinct from both null and zero, and set-oriented FOR EACH / FIND phrases that map to JPA queries. NOTE: no free/OSS Progress runtime exists (the AVM is proprietary), so source-execution behavioural equivalence is NOT available for this schema — verification relies on golden-dataset extraction scoring and property-based checks of the generated Java target, and this limitation is documented rather than stubbed.

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants the procedure/function must preserve across all valid inputs — the business rules a reviewer signs off on and the Java target must uphold.

claimKinds.label: Temp-table usage
claimKinds.description: ABL DEFINE TEMP-TABLE declares a process-scoped, in-memory relational table with typed fields and indexes — used for working sets, ProDataset payloads, and passing structured data between procedures. Java has no direct equivalent: the target is a List<Dto> / record class (+ an index emulation such as a Map keyed on the index fields, or a lightweight in-memory H2 table when the temp-table is queried relationally). Flag whether the temp-table is passed BY-REFERENCE / BY-VALUE between procedures (shapes the Java method signature).

fields.name: fields_summary
fields.doc: Field names/types and index(es), e.g. 'ttOrder: OrderNum(int, index), CustNum(int), Amount(decimal)'.

fields.name: passed_between_procedures
fields.doc: TEMP-TABLE ... BY-REFERENCE parameters couple procedures — shapes the Java method signature (shared collection vs return value).

fields.name: java_equivalent
fields.doc: Recommended Java form, e.g. 'List<OrderLine> record class' or 'in-memory H2 table via Spring Data' when queried relationally.

claimKinds.label: Shared / global variable scope
claimKinds.description: ABL DEFINE SHARED / NEW SHARED / GLOBAL variables (and shared buffers/temp-tables) create implicit cross-procedure coupling: a called procedure reads or mutates state the caller declared, with no parameter passing. This hidden data flow has no Java equivalent and is a frequent bug source. The Java target must make the dependency explicit — a passed parameter, a Spring-managed bean, or request-scoped state — never a static mutable field on a shared class.

fields.name: mutated
fields.doc: Whether this routine writes the shared variable (a side effect visible to other procedures).

claimKinds.label: Record phrase & lock semantics
claimKinds.description: ABL data-access phrases — FIND FIRST/LAST/NEXT, FOR EACH, CAN-FIND, GET FIRST — operate on implicit record buffers one row at a time, with an explicit lock mode (NO-LOCK read-only, SHARE-LOCK shared, EXCLUSIVE-LOCK for update). The lock mode and the record-at-a-time cursor model map to JPA semantics: NO-LOCK → a read-only query / @Transactional(readOnly=true); EXCLUSIVE-LOCK → a managed entity inside a write transaction with @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE); FOR EACH → a JPA query returning a stream/list. FIND with no record and no NO-ERROR raises; FIND ... NO-ERROR then AVAILABLE-check is the guarded pattern.

fields.name: phrase
fields.doc: The record phrase, e.g. 'FIND FIRST Customer WHERE ... EXCLUSIVE-LOCK'.

fields.name: jpa_equivalent
fields.doc: The Spring Data / JPA form, e.g. 'repository.findFirstByCustNum(..) read-only' or '@Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) managed entity'.

claimKinds.label: Transaction scope
claimKinds.description: ABL transactions are BLOCK-SCOPED, not explicit begin/commit: the transaction spans the outermost block that performs a database update (a DO TRANSACTION block, or implicitly the procedure/FOR-EACH block containing the first update). All updates in that block commit or roll back together; an UNDO reverses to the block start. This implicit, structural boundary must become an explicit Spring @Transactional boundary in Java, and the reviewer must confirm the scope (per-record vs per-batch) matches. Sub-transactions and SUBTRANSACTION blocks map to nested/REQUIRES_NEW propagation.

fields.name: scope_block
fields.doc: The block that defines the transaction boundary, e.g. 'DO TRANSACTION:' or 'the FOR EACH OrderLine block'.

fields.name: spring_equivalent
fields.doc: The @Transactional placement + propagation, e.g. '@Transactional on the batch method' or '@Transactional(propagation=REQUIRES_NEW) per record'.

claimKinds.label: Error handling contract
claimKinds.description: ABL error handling spans several styles that must all become Java exceptions: NO-ERROR (suppresses the error and sets ERROR-STATUS:ERROR / :GET-MESSAGE for the caller to check — a silent-failure trap if unchecked), classic ON ERROR / ON ENDKEY phrases, and modern structured CATCH ... END CATCH blocks (OpenEdge 10.1+). NO-ERROR without a following ERROR-STATUS check silently swallows failures. The Java target uses try/catch; every NO-ERROR must be classified as 'checked' (an AVAILABLE/ERROR-STATUS guard follows) or 'swallowed' (no guard — likely a latent bug the SME must confirm).

claimKinds.label: Side effect
claimKinds.description: Externally-visible state mutations: database writes (CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE / ASSIGN on a buffer), file I/O (OUTPUT TO / INPUT FROM), shared-variable mutation, RUN of an external .p/.w with side effects, DYNAMIC-FUNCTION calls, and OS-command execution (OS-COMMAND / OS-COPY).

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Boundary and semantic conditions specific to ABL → Java migration: the Unknown value (?) which is DISTINCT from null and from zero (a numeric field can be ? meaning 'no value', and ? propagates through arithmetic); ABL string comparison and keyword matching are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (unlike Java's case-sensitive equals); DECIMAL is a fixed-point type with defined rounding (not IEEE double); integer division truncates; the leave/next block-label control flow; and FIND that returns no record leaving the buffer NOT AVAILABLE (dereferencing it is an error).

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Ambiguities that require SME resolution. Common ABL cases: character/GUI UI (FRAME / DISPLAY / FORM / SmartWindow .w files) has no server-side Java equivalent and must be re-platformed separately; RUN ... PERSISTENT procedure-handle lifecycle → decide the Spring bean/object lifecycle; {include.i} preprocessor includes and &GLOBAL-DEFINE macros must be resolved before the target is complete; the physical database schema behind buffer names must be mapped to JPA entities; and DYNAMIC-FUNCTION / dynamic query strings need a chosen Java strategy.

topLevelFields.name: enclosing_type
topLevelFields.doc: The .p/.w program or the internal PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/METHOD name.

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: ABL parameter modes. INPUT (default) = by value; OUTPUT = returned to caller; INPUT-OUTPUT = by reference; BUFFER / TABLE / TABLE-HANDLE = record/temp-table parameters; return = the FUNCTION return value.

promptHints.emphasis: Every DEFINE TEMP-TABLE is a tempTableUsage claim (note BY-REFERENCE parameters). Every DEFINE SHARED / NEW SHARED / GLOBAL variable is a sharedVariableScope claim — hidden cross-procedure coupling. Every FIND / FOR EACH / CAN-FIND is a recordPhraseSemantics claim; ALWAYS capture the lock mode (NO-LOCK / SHARE-LOCK / EXCLUSIVE-LOCK) because it dictates the JPA transaction/lock. Every DB update establishes a transactionScope — identify the block that bounds it. Every NO-ERROR is an errorHandlingContract; classify checked vs swallowed. Treat the Unknown value (?) and ABL's default case-insensitivity as edgeCase claims. FRAME/DISPLAY UI, RUN PERSISTENT lifecycle, and {include.i} resolution are openQuestions.

calibratedAgainst: Tier-2 OpenEdge ABL portfolio (2 apps, talent-extinction risk)
